rows.grounds: Sandhi-fused form: mantradevān (mantra-deva, accusative plural) + tataḥ (then); refers to the deities of the mantras.
The ritual practitioner who employs the mantra.
Sandhi-fused form: dhyāyet (optative of dhyai, to meditate) + susthira-mānasaḥ (bahuvrīhi adjective, having a very steady mind).

items.question: What mental condition must the mantrin maintain while meditating on the mantra-deities?
premises: The preceding context identifies the bīja and śakti to be employed.
The mantrin is directed to meditate on the mantra-deities thereafter.
The meditation is to be performed with a very steady mind.
items.inference: Effective meditation on the mantra-deities requires the mantrin to maintain a very steady mind.
uncertainties: The exact scope of mantradevān (specific deities or deities in general) depends on the preceding ritual context.
items.plain_english: Then the mantrin, with a very steady mind, should meditate on the deities of the mantras.
